candidates.tagline: NZ Football misspelled 'Egypt' as 'EYGPT' on their official World Cup pennant
candidates.story: Before their June 21, 2026 FIFA World Cup Group G match in Vancouver, New Zealand Football presented Egypt with a ceremonial pennant that spelled the country's name 'EYGPT' in large capital letters — and didn't notice until after the match.
candidates.why_funny: They spent months preparing for their first World Cup match in 40+ years, had an official pennant printed, and nobody in the entire federation checked how to spell 'Egypt.'
candidates.alt: Official FIFA World Cup '26 ceremonial pennant hanging in New Zealand's locker room reading 'NEW ZEALAND vs EYGPT — 21ST JUNE 2026 — VANCOUVER, CANADA' with the misspelling visible in large capital letters

candidates.tagline: Google's first new speaker in 6 years has a hardwired cable you can never replace
candidates.story: The Google Home Speaker, Google's first new smart speaker in six years, launched June 25, 2026 with a permanently attached USB-C power cable — there is no port on the device, so if the cable (the most fragile component) breaks, the $99 speaker cannot be repaired without opening the case.
candidates.why_funny: Six years of development time and not a single engineer added a cable port — every previous Google speaker had a removable cord, making this the first that turns a frayed cable into a landfill trip.
candidates.alt: Google Home Speaker in Jade green with rainbow LED touch-control lights at its base and a white USB-C power cable permanently exiting from the lower-back of the unit with no visible port to disconnect it
